sections.heading: Buy-to-let deposit and LTV (from /faq/, [a][b][seed])
sections.content: Most BTL products max out at 75% LTV, requiring a 25% deposit from the borrower. This varies by lender; lender, borrower profile and property type can push the deposit higher. HMO products: typically 75% LTV, some lenders 80% in exceptional circumstances (seed).

sections.heading: Regulation / consumer buy-to-let (from Ts&Cs and /faq/, [a][b][seed])
sections.content: Buy-to-let mortgages are not normally regulated by the FCA; some are 'consumer buy-to-let', which the firm says it will advise on / flag during the application. The major determining factor is whether the borrower intends to live in the property after the mortgage has completed. Seed adds: if the borrower or a family member occupies more than 40% of the property, it becomes a regulated loan.

sections.heading: Landlord experience / first-time landlords (from /faq/, [a][seed])
sections.content: Most lenders prefer the borrower to have owned a standard buy-to-let for at least 12 months (context: before buying an HMO). The firm works with several lenders who permit first-time landlords to buy HMOs provided strong personal income and a clear management plan.

sections.heading: Portfolio landlords (from /faq/, [seed])
sections.content: A portfolio loan can sit alongside existing individual mortgages; the premium on portfolio products has narrowed. (From seed only; not re-surfaced in this run.)

sections.heading: Fees and remuneration (from Ts&Cs, /lenders/, [a][seed])
sections.content: Fees and charges are set out in a client-specific Fee Agreement. The firm typically receives commission from lenders, disclosed during the process (seed /lenders/). No BTL-specific fee figure recovered.

faq.q: How much deposit do I need for a buy-to-let mortgage?
faq.a: Most BTL products will max out at 75% LTV, requiring a deposit from the borrower of 25% of the property's value. This varies by lender however; the lender, borrower profile and property type can push the deposit higher. (/faq/, [a][b][seed])

faq.q: Can a first-time landlord buy an HMO?
faq.a: Most lenders prefer you to have owned a standard buy-to-let for at least 12 months, but the firm works with several lenders who permit first-time landlords to buy HMOs provided strong personal income and a clear management plan. (/faq/, [a][seed])

faq.q: Is a buy-to-let mortgage regulated by the FCA?
faq.a: Not normally; some are 'consumer buy-to-let' and the firm will advise/flag if that applies. The major determining factor is whether the borrower intends to live in the property after the mortgage has been signed and completed. If you or a family member occupies more than 40% of the property, it becomes a regulated loan. (Ts&Cs + /faq/, [a][b][seed])

faq.q: Can a portfolio loan sit alongside existing mortgages?
faq.a: Yes, a portfolio loan can sit alongside existing individual mortgages; the premium on portfolio products has narrowed. (/faq/, [seed])
All details surrounding fees and charges will be highlighted in the Client specific Fee Agreement. (Ts&Cs, [a])
